leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations are a single prize part on B004 (GLP-1 and incretin therapy). They share Drucker and Holst and a physiology-to-medicine rationale resting on independent randomised outcome trials. They differ on the third name and the citation scope: five members name Mojsov with a discovery-centred citation (physiology and the bioactive peptide), while El-Manira names Knudsen with a citation that spans physiology and drug development. Linnarsson moved from his opening trio to the Mojsov set after reading colleagues' attribution arguments, and El-Manira moved from B007 first to B004. Habener is outside the credited names and several members flag his priority as unresolved.

areas_of_agreement: All six members explicitly prefer B004 as the single prize part in their round-1 configurations.
All six describe the B004 discovery chain as original, mechanistically clear, independently replicated and mature, with no maturity objection stated.
All six say the weak point of B004 is attribution and not scientific merit, and that the three-laureate limit makes any B004 trio partial.
Five of six members (all but El-Manira) share the same laureate trio of Drucker, Holst and Mojsov.

Four members (Linnarsson, Sandberg, Wahren-Herlenius, Svenningsson) list B018 and B043 as alternatives, and El-Manira and Perlmann each share one of them (B043 and B018 respectively), so alternatives are scattered and no second prize part has an explicit majority.
Several members note that the shortlist's credited names for B018 and B043 each leave a visible attribution gap (Eshhar for CAR-T, six names for three places in optogenetics).
scientific_disputes: Whether B004 should be framed as physiology and discovery of the active peptide, or as physiology plus the development of long-acting analogues. Perlmann and Sandberg prefer to keep the citation in the discovery domain, El-Manira prefers a span to drug development.

Whether a tool such as optogenetics (B043) is sufficiently medicine-oriented, given that its clinical translation is early and its case rests on research impact (raised by Wahren-Herlenius, El-Manira and Svenningsson).
Whether the unfolded protein response (B032) is a strong pure-mechanism candidate, with clean attribution but only developing direct clinical consequences (Perlmann, Svenningsson).
Whether SMN2 antisense (B047) is a clean mechanism-to-medicine chain or a narrower rare-disease story with competing therapies (Linnarsson, Svenningsson).
attribution_disputes: Third name for B004: Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, preferred by five members) versus Knudsen (long-acting analogues, preferred by El-Manira and noted as a significant omission by every other member).

Habener is not among the credited names, yet members cite his group's proglucagon and GLP-1 work as a possible priority claim against Mojsov. Nobody says this can be resolved from the supplied record.

B018 (CAR-T): Eshhar, originator of the chimeric receptor concept, is absent from the credited names, and the three names split into receptor design, clinical translation and a broader adoptive cell therapy line (Sandberg, Perlmann, Wahren-Herlenius).

B043 (optogenetics): six credited names for three places, with Nagel and Hegemann (channelrhodopsin), Deisseroth (neuronal implementation), Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck all having claims (Wahren-Herlenius).

B007 (imatinib): El-Manira notes the upstream discoveries (Philadelphia chromosome, BCR-ABL) sit outside the credited trio. Svenningsson makes the same point and adds the Lasker 2009 recognition of the group.
maturity_disputes: No member raises a maturity objection to B004. The maturity discussion concerns the alternatives.
Wahren-Herlenius calls B043 mature and overdue as a method, whereas Svenningsson accepts maturity but qualifies 'overdue' because clinical translation is early.
El-Manira treats B007 (imatinib) as mature and arguably overdue, but Svenningsson does not regard that as outweighing B004, given the earlier Lasker recognition and the incomplete origin story.
Perlmann and Svenningsson note the direct disease consequences of the B032 unfolded protein response are still developing, though basic maturity is not in question.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Svenningsson discloses about twenty co-authored works with Perlmann and a postdoctoral link to Paul Greengard. Neither involves a shortlisted candidate.
Perlmann discloses the same co-authorship with Svenningsson and one co-authorship with El-Manira (2009). Neither involves a shortlisted candidate.
El-Manira discloses shared work with Perlmann (2009), Grillner and Ernfors. None is a credited shortlist name. He notes that his circuit neuroscience field is nearest to B043 and B047.
Sandberg discloses co-authorship with Linnarsson and Frisén. None of the shortlisted candidates is credited.
Wahren-Herlenius notes that her field (autoimmunity) is adjacent to B018 but gives no personal tie to the credited names.
Linnarsson reports no candidate-specific conflict but says he has not checked this against every candidate's full publication record.
No member reports a recusal-level conflict for any shortlisted candidate.
questions_for_round2: Should the third B004 laureate be Mojsov or Knudsen, and what documentary evidence in the supplied record bears on Mojsov's priority relative to Habener?
Should the B004 citation honour physiology and discovery of the bioactive peptide only, or span to drug development, and how would each wording change the credited trio?
If Habener's priority claim cannot be resolved, should the citation wording carry the uncertainty, or should it affect the choice of laureates?
Is a second prize part worthwhile, given that a two-part prize would cap the union at three people and reduce the B004 trio, and if so which alternative (B018, B043, B032, B047 or B007) is strongest?
Can B018 (CAR-T) be credited fairly without Eshhar, and is Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer distinct enough from CAR design to support a three-person allocation?
Can B043 (optogenetics) be allocated among six credited people, and does a research tool meet the committee's medicine-oriented standard?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows unusually strong alignment: all six explicit configurations are a single B004 prize part, and the open issue is the third laureate and citation scope. Five members name the same trio and one names Knudsen instead. All six say the unresolved priority question involving Habener cannot be settled from the supplied record. Member arguments for B004 rest on the science rather than on the opening-ballot count. The alternatives (B018, B043, B032, B047, B007) are scattered and none has an explicit majority position.
